stem: Which compartment of the ruminant stomach is the glandular (true) stomach that secretes HCl and pepsinogen?
explanation: The abomasum is the only glandular compartment; the first three are forestomachs lined with non-glandular epithelium.
source: Author draft by Claude (2026-11-18), unverified. Verify against: a veterinary physiology or animal nutrition text, digestive chapter (lesson-rum-001)

stem: Which volatile fatty acid is the main precursor for glucose synthesis in the liver of ruminants?
explanation: Propionate is absorbed from the rumen and converted to glucose by hepatic gluconeogenesis. Acetate mainly supports fat synthesis; butyrate is largely converted to ketone bodies by the rumen wall; lactate is not a VFA.
source: Author draft by Claude (2026-11-18), unverified. Verify against: a veterinary physiology or animal nutrition text, digestive chapter (lesson-rum-001)

stem: A cow suddenly eats a large amount of grain. Which change in the rumen is most likely?

choices.text: Rumen pH rises because saliva output increases
Rumination increases because more coarse fiber is eaten
Rapid fermentation of starch lowers the rumen pH (acidosis)

explanation: Rapidly fermentable starch produces acids faster than the rumen can buffer them, so pH falls and cellulose-digesting microbes are suppressed.
source: Author draft by Claude (2026-11-18), unverified. Verify against: a veterinary physiology or animal nutrition text, digestive chapter (lesson-rum-001)

stem: A cow swallows a nail. In which compartment is the object most likely to lodge?
explanation: Heavy foreign bodies settle in the reticulum, whose honeycomb lining and contractions can drive them through the wall (hardware disease).

stem: In a suckling calf, milk bypasses the undeveloped rumen and reaches the abomasum because of the:

stem: Which animal is classified as a hind-gut fermenter?
